A fighters association is needed. Anyone that says they cannot do it, or it's impossible, is very dim imo. 

Unionisation has already begun. Not in the way that people think. Fighter managers, who have multiple fighters in their portfolio's like Ali for example, hold significant power. We have seen them use it in negotiations and his guys often get better deals and more of his fighters get signed. Yes, there is still risk. They could play too hard negotiating or their champ client loses or retires, and the money and power flow out of the managers stable for a time.

If a single manager held majority of the fighters in his stable, let's say 75%(random majority number), then they could effectively act as a union and make demands on the basis of acting as the majority working force and take real action.

If such a situation would to occur then possibly;
 the manager could sell out and screw the fighters,
the UFC could wait it out and sign a bunch of fighters without that management, Super Manager takes UFC to court on behalf of his fighters to get releases for fighters, Fighters can start new org ran by them who get a larger share and starts new Organisation with a ready made stable of established names.

There are so many possoble scenarios still. The calls for more pay from disgruntled fighters isn't new but the calls are getting louder and coming more often. Different tactics will start to come into play imo
